title: Surgical pool patching with capacity hedging and autoscaler contracts
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: introduce a low-risk 'surgical patch' upgrade workflow for dedicated GPU pools that combines small, targeted node-side updates with short-duration hedged capacity reservations and an explicit autoscaler contract. This ticket defines the orchestration, telemetry, and fallback behavior so that rolling patches to device drivers, micro-kernels, or runtime libs do not cause tenant request surges or SLA violations.
acceptance_criteria: Patch orchestration can update up to 5% of a pool at once while maintaining 99th percentile latency within the pool SLA for normal load
Autoscaler contract (handshake) prevents scale-to-zero or aggressive downscales during a patch window
Canary slices are exercised for model inference across representative tenants and rollback is automatic on error rate spike > 4x baseline
Telemetry dashboard shows pre/post token cost, queue depth, and soft-failure counts for the patched slice
Runbook documented and dry-run tested in staging with a simulated tenant mix
steps: Design autoscaler contract: introduce patch-window hint + min-hedge tokens in the autoscaler API
Implement controller to create 'surgical slice' (small subset of nodes) and tag with patch metadata
Add short-lived capacity hedges: reserve N ephemeral slots per tenant tier during the patch window
Route a configurable 2-5% of live traffic to the canary slice via traffic-weights at the routing layer
Execute runtime/driver patch on canary slice with KV-cache warmup and prefilled prefixes
Monitor custom SLOs for 30 minutes; if thresholds exceed, trigger automated rollback and increase hedge
If stable, progressively expand patch windows in 5% increments with 10–20 minute observation periods
Post-patch: drain hedges over 1 hour and reconcile autoscaler min/max settings
risks_mitigation: Risk: Autoscaler ignores hint and shrinks capacity -> Mitigation: require API-level ACK from autoscaler; controller will freeze scale actions for the slice
Risk: Traffic spike due to tenant retries -> Mitigation: apply per-tenant admission backpressure and request-shedding thresholds during patch window
Risk: Quiescing KV-cache causes latency tail -> Mitigation: pre-warm KV-cache with synthetic prefixes and measure hit-rate before routing real traffic
Risk: Patch causes device driver hangs on a small subset -> Mitigation: rapid rollback path + circuit-breaker that isolates failing nodes and marks them for manual review
